| PHASE4:MAL-TCP-CUT-00 / MAL-TCP-CUT-00 | RFC 9293 §3.1, RFC 791 §3.1 | implementation-profile / PROFILE | TCP base header, Data Offset, options and checksum must describe an available segment. Illegal option lengths must be handled gracefully (MUST-7); reset is recommended, not required. Exact-buffer safety and recovery are robustness properties. [existing-requirement-paraphrase; PROFILE may include local robustness conditions] | IPv4 over Ethernet; native input path; exact-size receive allocation; fabricated TCP fixture | No application delivery from malformed input, no sanitizer error, then valid TCP bytes and UDP length/first byte in the same workspace. Each case isolated; diagnostics identify physical length and recovery outcomes. Recovery is compared with a fresh same-state clean TCP/UDP control. A matching recovery with a failing clean control is INCONCLUSIVE and names MAL-VALID-*; malformed delivery/state/silence violations and differential recovery remain FAIL. Oracle: white-box; Byte-built malformed input; placed TCP state and same-state clean control compare wire, callbacks and internal state. UDP callbacks observe length/first byte, not a complete application stream. No option-error adapter enabled. | partial / unreported | Finite input set; ASan/UBSan success is not a proof of memory safety. No leak assertion. See README.md#malformed-input-and-recovery for reset policy, maximum lengths and callback limits. |
